_what: Branch's look. Started from keep/link and keep/gauge so it read as one of the family, then moved off the family's green to soft whites and blues at his instruction. The structure -- theme as data, ui_scale, slab-and-tray -- is still the family's.
_rule: No red anywhere, by house rule. No magenta or purple either -- the first draft of this window had both and they were wrong.
_trays: No outlines anywhere. A control is a tray: a slightly darker, slightly transparent slab that the text sits on. Hovering makes it less transparent rather than adding a border. Selected uses the accent tint, still with no edge.
_font: Ubuntu Sans is installed on this machine; Inter is not, so link's stylesheet has been falling back to DejaVu Sans without saying so. Never name a weight inside a family: fontconfig substitutes silently.
_scale: Every measurement in the window is authored small and multiplied by this before it reaches the screen, so one value here makes the whole window bigger or smaller without changing a single number in the code. Same mechanism as gauge's page_scale. This is separate from DPI: Qt already scales for the monitor, this is taste.
_glass: Frost, not tint. The window was reading as black because the slab was a near-black ground colour: lowering its alpha only made a dark pane paler. A frosted pane is a light veil over a blurred backdrop, so the slab is now a mid blue-grey and the trays are a light wash (like keep/link's rgba(foreground,.03)) rather than dark holes. picom supplies the blur and then its own 0.96/0.88 on top.
_corners: picom.conf sets corner-radius = 10 globally on this desktop. Ours must match it EXACTLY: picom cuts the blur at 10, so painting a 12 curve left the blur showing through outside our edge and the corner clipped badly. Same number, no artefact.
_text: Pulled back from link's #EAF0ED, which glares against a low-alpha slab. The family's value assumes a more opaque window than this one.
